request.what: Reduce the committeeMinSize protocol parameter from 7 to 5.

claims.claim: The proposal changes the minimum Constitutional Committee size parameter, committeeMinSize, from 7 to 5.
The current Constitutional Committee has 7 members, equal to the current committeeMinSize of 7.

If the number of Constitutional Committee members drops below committeeMinSize, governance actions requiring Constitutional Committee approval become ineligible for ratification, including Parameter Changes, Constitution Updates, Treasury Withdrawals, and Hard Forks.
Reducing committeeMinSize to 5 would create an operational buffer so governance can continue if one or two members retire or their terms expire, assuming a 7-member body.

The proposal depends temporally on another live Parameter Change governance action for Plutus cost model updates before the van Rossem hard fork, but states there is no technical interaction between the two parameter changes.
The proposal does not directly change the current number of Constitutional Committee members or the maximum number of Constitutional Committee members.
With a 2/3 Constitutional Committee voting threshold, a 5-member committee would require 4 constitutional votes to meet threshold and 2 unconstitutional votes to prevent threshold.
The proposal states that at a Constitutional Committee size of 5, inactivity by one member would allow another member to fully veto governance actions.
The proposal states that the change passed the Parameter Committee Parameter Change Process and satisfies guardrails requiring committeeMinSize to be nonnegative, at least 3, and not above 10.

The proposal includes a reversion plan stating that returning committeeMinSize to 7 is reversible if at least 7 Constitutional Committee members exist, but would halt governance if fewer than 7 members existed at reversion.

summary: The document proposes a non-treasury parameter change to lower committeeMinSize from 7 to 5, arguing this improves governance resilience against member departures while preserving constitutional safeguards, and it acknowledges a tradeoff that smaller committee sizes make vetoes easier.
